item.title: MATLAB Performance: Vectorization vs Loop Optimization
item.description:
“MATLAB Performance: Vectorization vs Loop Optimization”

The goal is to determine the most efficient strategy when the computation is memory bandwidth bounded and the underlying operation is simple.

Performance Benchmarks for Scalar Function Application

Consider an initial setup where we are applying a simple polynomial function element-wise to an input matrix $x$ of size $T \times N$.

Observation 1: Overhead of Function Calls within Loops

Using an anonymous function inside a tight, doubly nested loop shows significant performance penalties compared to direct computation.

item.title: R Vectorized Conditional Logic: Alternatives to Standard If-Else for Vector Operations
item.description:
“R Vectorized Conditional Logic: Alternatives to Standard If-Else for Vector Operations”

When working with vectors in R, standard if statements behave differently than in procedural languages because they are not inherently vectorized. Applying a condition like a > 0 to a vector a yields a logical vector (TRUE/FALSE). Using this directly in a standard if context can lead to warnings or unexpected results because if expects a single truth value. How can we apply element-wise conditional transformations efficiently?
